Field

One labelled control, a text input, a textarea or a select, with its description and its error message.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For one line of text the reader types: a name, a path, a branch, a search term.
  • Around a textarea or a select, which take their label, description and error from the field.
  • Whenever a control needs a label, which is always.

When not to use it

  • With a bare text input for more than one line of text. Use a textarea as the field's control.
  • With a bare text input for a choice from a fixed list. Use a select as the field's control.
  • For the prompt under a transcript. Use a composer.
  • For a value the reader cannot change but will copy. Use a copy field.
  • For a value the reader cannot change and never needs to copy. Write it as plain text.

Sizes

default
The control is 44px tall and as wide as the field. Limit the width on the field's container.

Accessibility

  • Every control has a label element whose for attribute matches the control's id. A placeholder is not a label.
  • Mark a required control with the required attribute and the word required in the label. Never use colour or an asterisk alone.
  • Link the description, and the error while there is one, by listing their ids in aria-describedby on the control.
  • For an invalid value, set aria-invalid="true" on the control and add the error element. Remove both when the value is fixed.
  • The error message says how to fix the value. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet, so it needs no markup.
  • A read-only control stays focusable and its text can be copied. A disabled one leaves the tab order.
